headline: Microsoft AI Frontiers group disbanded after leadership clash
summary: Microsoft's AI research unit, AI Frontiers, has been dissolved following a strategic disagreement with the newly formed Microsoft AI division, led by former Inflection AI executives.
details: Microsoft's AI Frontiers (AIF) sub-organization within Microsoft Research, established to foster more organized AI research, has reportedly been disbanded. The group, comprising around 50 researchers, focused on developing agentic AI capabilities and fundamental research, including projects like the Autogen orchestration framework and the Full Bandwidth Transformer.

The dissolution follows a reorg into Microsoft AI in early September. While consolidation can offer benefits, AIF leadership found the core philosophy of the new Microsoft AI division, led by former Inflection AI executives, to be incompatible. This new division reportedly prioritizes aggressive scaling over research.

The AIF team's research-focused approach clashed with the new division's emphasis on scaling and data refinement. This divergence in philosophy, coupled with perceived unfriendliness towards the AIF team, led to significant issues.

John Langford, a key figure in AIF, stated that the scaling-only focus is 'misdirected and not fun,' emphasizing that research yields significant returns. He cited experiments suggesting a variant of the Full Bandwidth Transformer could match a model twice its size, potentially saving trillions in training and inference costs.

Langford and other founding AIF leadership members have left the organization due to these philosophical differences. He noted that the compute bottleneck was also a persistent challenge for the group.

The article suggests that the 'scaling-only' approach is a failure mode where companies abandon the tradeoff between innovation and size by adopting one extreme. However, Langford expressed optimism about finding opportunities with others who value research and innovation.

headline_marked: [[$10 OpenStick]] Runs Debian, Podman, and AI Agents for a Tiny Homelab
headline: $10 OpenStick Runs Debian, Podman, and AI Agents for a Tiny Homelab
summary: Discover how a $10 OpenStick can be transformed into a functional homelab server running Debian, Podman, and various useful services like AdGuard Home and an AI agent harness.
details: For just $10, the OpenStick offers a surprisingly capable platform for self-hosting. It runs Debian, bringing classic Linux tools like systemd and Podman for containerization, all with minimal power usage and zero noise.
One of the useful applications is a sponsorship skipper for Google Cast devices, enhancing the YouTube experience by removing ads with minimal resource consumption.

AdGuard Home is implemented to block malicious domains at the DNS level, significantly reducing exposure to spyware and malware. With custom blocklists, it can block up to 60% of queries, offering a robust layer of security.

Zeroclaw, an AI agent harness, is also integrated. It supports multiple communication channels like Telegram and email, and uses minimal resources (~3 MB RSS idle), making it ideal for monitoring the OpenStick's status and logs remotely.
Cloudflared is used to securely expose these services to the internet without opening any ports, providing a free and convenient way to access your homelab from anywhere.

Beszel offers a visual dashboard for monitoring memory and CPU usage, sending alerts to Telegram when suspicious activity is detected. It's a lightweight alternative to heavier monitoring solutions like Grafana.
Dozzle provides a user-friendly interface for managing Podman containers, offering similar functionality to Beszel and potentially allowing for resource savings if one of the tools is removed.
caption:
Who knew a $10 device could run a full Linux homelab? This OpenStick is packed with Debian, Podman, and even AI agents!

For just $10, the OpenStick offers a surprisingly capable platform for self-hosting. It runs Debian, bringing classic Linux tools like systemd and Podman for containerization, all with minimal power usage and zero noise.

One of the useful applications is a sponsorship skipper for Google Cast devices, enhancing the YouTube experience by removing ads with minimal resource consumption.

AdGuard Home is implemented to block malicious domains at the DNS level, significantly reducing exposure to spyware and malware. With custom blocklists, it can block up to 60% of queries, offering a robust layer of security.

Zeroclaw, an AI agent harness, is also integrated. It supports multiple communication channels like Telegram and email, and uses minimal resources (~3 MB RSS idle), making it ideal for monitoring the OpenStick's status and logs remotely.

Cloudflared is used to securely expose these services to the internet without opening any ports, providing a free and convenient way to access your homelab from anywhere.

Beszel offers a visual dashboard for monitoring memory and CPU usage, sending alerts to Telegram when suspicious activity is detected. It's a lightweight alternative to heavier monitoring solutions like Grafana.

Dozzle provides a user-friendly interface for managing Podman containers, offering similar functionality to Beszel and potentially allowing for resource savings if one of the tools is removed.
